title: On the convergence of derivative-free methods for unconstrained optimization
contribution: Defines a broad class of interpolation-model trust-region DFO methods (Newton fundamental polynomials, Sauer-Xu error bound) and proves every limit point is first-order critical, with geometry adequacy gating radius reduction and a criticality loop tying model accuracy to the model gradient.
problem_entry: Practitioner demand for expensive simulations; direct search, AD and FD ruled out; Powell's interpolation methods worked numerically (Conn-Toint 1996, Powell 1996) but had no convergence theory (pp. 2-5).
key_idea: Keep the trust-region skeleton; shrink the radius only if the interpolation set is adequate (fully linear, bounded Newton polynomials), re-certify the model in a ball of radius <= mu*||g_k|| when g_k is small, and allow moves to the best interpolation point (pp. 14-15, 17-18).
assumptions: f C^2 with globally bounded gradient and Hessian, bounded below, bounded model Hessians (chosen 'to keep our analysis simple', p. 6); adequacy = >= n+1 points in the ball with bounded Newton polynomials (p. 11); no noise, unconstrained.
proof_devices: Sauer-Xu path-sum interpolation error bound (3.8) (p. 9)
constructive well-poised set: each point = argmax of current Newton polynomial over the ball; normalization + at-most-doubling gives bound 2^{|Y[d]|} (Theorem 2, pp. 10-11)
function-error to gradient-error transfer by Taylor + direction h = delta*(grad f - g)/||grad f - g|| (Theorem 4, pp. 12-13)
criticality loop finiteness by geometric shrinking and triangle inequality (Lemma 5(iii), pp. 16-17)
radius bounded below away from criticality by first-reduction contradiction using adequacy at reductions (Lemma 7, pp. 18-19)
standard TR skeleton: liminf via summed Cauchy decrease, all limit points via sum-of-radii argument (Theorems 9-12, pp. 19-22)
experiments: none (numerics deferred to Conn-Toint 1996 and Powell 1996, p. 5)
positioning: Full section on Powell's DFO contributions as 'the main source of our inspiration'; Newton instead of Lagrange polynomials justified by the Sauer-Xu formula, not superiority; Carter 1991 and More 1983 as TR theory (pp. 4-7, 15, 18).
writing: Modest ('reasonable global convergence results', 'admittedly simplistic', 'merely to explore a framework'); plain-language paragraphs after key lemmas; flags own Lemma 3 as 'of little theoretical use' and geometry constant as theory-only (pp. 2, 11-12, 15, 17, 19).
limits_future: Future: which class members perform best numerically, extend the class, bounds other than Sauer-Xu (p. 22). Unstated: no rates/complexity, global gradient bound, no algorithmic adequacy test via pivots (p. 12), costly full-set geometry repair (criticized in S016 p. 19).

title: A derivative free optimization algorithm in practice
contribution: Practice paper for the Conn-Scheinberg-Toint DFO code: prose algorithm, practical properties (fully linear suffices, min-Frobenius models, noise robustness), a three-class constraint treatment (easy / difficult / virtual-hidden), and evaluation-count comparisons with PDS, LANCELOT-FD and COBYLA on CUTE/HS plus a Boeing helicopter application.
problem_entry: Engineering black boxes (Boeing helicopter rotor with 11-50 variables at ~1 min/evaluation, engine nozzle at hours/evaluation, water-network calibration); goal: few evaluations, use each value as soon as available (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Interpolation trust region that decreases the radius only once the model is fully linear, grows the model from 2 points, uses minimum-Frobenius-norm underdetermined models, and puts cheap constraints exactly into the subproblem (pp. 3-7).
assumptions: f C^2, derivatives unavailable, expensive, noise typically present, n < 100; constraints defined by smooth functions even if unknown; hidden constraints assumed to be smooth feasible sets (pp. 2, 6, 8).
proof_devices: none new; convergence cited to S008 with the remark that fully linear suffices (p. 5)
counting argument: 528 points for one full quadratic in 31 variables vs good solution after ~180 evaluations (p. 5)
informal noise argument: noise matters only when trust-region radius is small relative to noise; FD gradients fragile if noise level unknown (pp. 5-6)
counter-picture for own virtual-constraint heuristic (Figure 1, pp. 7-8)
experiments: 26 unconstrained CUTE, 13 inequality-HS, 16 equality-HS problems vs PDS, LANCELOT-FD, COBYLA; function evaluations and final f, CPU time explicitly omitted, tolerances not matched; LANCELOT-FD fewer evaluations on 16/26 unconstrained, DFO fewer on 12/13 and 15/16 constrained (my count); helicopter 10 restarts per size with 15-20% failed evaluations counted (pp. 8-11).
positioning: Algorithm of S008/S004 with Conn-Toint 1996 prototype and Powell inspiration; baselines span direct search, FD quasi-Newton (own LANCELOT), Powell's COBYLA; Booker et al. 1998 for helicopter comparisons (pp. 3, 8, 11).
writing: Practice voice, prose algorithm, hedged claims about global minima, names the flaw of its own heuristic, no conclusion section (pp. 3-5, 8, 11).
limits_future: Virtual-constraint heuristic can stop at non-minimizers; difficult constraints left to ongoing research; local convergence only; future: more sophisticated heuristics (pp. 5, 7-8). Unstated: no equal-accuracy protocol; unconstrained LANCELOT wins not discussed.

title: Efficient SVM training using low-rank kernel representations
contribution: Makes an interior point method for the SVM dual QP run in O(nk^2) time and O(nk) storage when the kernel has (or is approximated by) rank k, via product-form Cholesky updates and greedy pivoted incomplete Cholesky, with a method-agnostic bound c^2*l*eps/2 on the optimal-value change.
problem_entry: SVM QP scales with n and a general IPM iteration is O(n^3); existing remedies decompose into small subproblems; new entry is the numerical rank of the kernel matrix, stated as three key observations (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Keep Mehrotra's IPM and change only the linear algebra of (D + VV^T)^{-1}w: product-form Cholesky instead of SMW because the IPM drives D to ill-conditioning near optimality; approximate full-rank kernels by pivoted incomplete Cholesky with a free trace stopping rule (pp. 2, 5-14).
assumptions: PSD dense kernel of rank k << n (or approximable); scalar c for simplicity; fast spectral decay typical; Theorem 1 needs Q - Q~ PSD with trace <= eps; PFC stability proof not extended from LP to SVM QP ('beyond interest of this paper') (pp. 2, 4, 12, 15).
proof_devices: operation counts per solve: SMW nk^2/2 vs PFC k^2n (pp. 7, 11)
2x2 machine-precision example showing SMW failure (Example 1, pp. 7-8) plus complementarity argument that IPM produces that scaling (p. 8)
trace identity: sum of remaining pivoted-Cholesky diagonals = tr(residual) (p. 14)
perturbation sandwich on a shared feasible set: f~(x~*) <= f~(x*) <= f(x*) and f(x*) - f~(x~*) <= 1/2 x~*^T dQ x~* <= c^2 l eps/2 (Theorem 1, pp. 14-15)
experiments: CPU time vs dot-product-specialised SMO on 150 speaker-ID problems (n ~ 7000) and vs SVMlight across chunk sizes on Abalone; SMW vs PFC digits of accuracy on constructed and real instances; ICF effect on objective, ||w||, train/test error vs rank on Abalone poly kernel; competitor tolerances not stated (pp. 15-20).
positioning: Against decomposition methods (SMO, chunking, shrinking) and random-sampling low-rank approximations (Smola-Schoelkopf, Williams-Seeger); imports LP-IPM linear algebra (Goldfarb-Scheinberg 1999, SMW trouble in LP); notation section bridges optimization and SVM conventions (pp. 1-4, 7, 9, 12).
writing: Contribution as three numbered observations; generality of the bound advertised in the abstract; trade-offs stated both ways (SMW preferable if accuracy is not a priority); gaps admitted (pp. 1-2, 12, 18-19).
limits_future: Future: embed in chunking/shrinking for massive data, use approximate problem to identify support vectors then re-solve, bound ensuring active-set identification (pp. 19-20). Unstated: no competitor tolerances; timing shown with exactly low-rank dot-product kernels (my inference).

title: An efficient implementation of an active set method for SVMs
contribution: Shows that a classical full dual active-set QP method, adapted to SVM structure (one-index working-set changes with O(n_s^2) Cholesky updates, singular-case infinite directions, LP-style pricing with sprint), beats SVMlight in CPU time, and releases it as open-source SVM-QP.
problem_entry: Dense high-rank SVM kernels defeat IPMs; full active-set methods were considered impractical for large SVMs; chunking/decomposition are slow near the optimum and sensitive to an unpredictable chunk size (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Keep the simplex-type active-set method; take one step toward the reduced-QP solution per iteration, change the active set one index at a time so the Cholesky factor of Q_ss is updated not refactorized, and price reduced costs by the most negative element using sprint or shrinking (pp. 3, 5-14).
assumptions: Standard soft-margin SVM with any nonnegative penalty vector; Q_ss may be singular; number of margin support vectors moderate (if n_s ~ n the method is impractical and the problem likely overfits); Q_s storable (<= 400 MB) (pp. 1, 7, 10, 13).
proof_devices: no new convergence proof; finite termination inherited from Fletcher 1971 / Frangioni 1996, worst case exponential (p. 4)
Schur complement for the bias and triangular solves for the free variables (pp. 6-7)
infinite descent directions read from the zero rows of a singular Cholesky factor, verified by substitution (Cases 1-3, pp. 7-9)
structural argument: more than two zero eigenvalues only from warm starts since each infinite-direction step removes one index (p. 8)
bordered Cholesky add and Givens-rotation delete in O(n_s^2) (pp. 9-10)
experiments: Letter-G, USPS OCR, Web, Adult, Abalone, Spam with RBF/linear/poly kernels and several C; CPU seconds with equal memory; SVMlight run at default 1e-3 and at SVM-QP's 1e-6; full Adult/Web re-run by a third party (Mittelmann) incl. own out-of-memory failure; ablations sprint vs shrinking, memory-saving mode, IPM warm start (not dramatic), incremental mode (much slower) (pp. 10-19).
positioning: Descends from simplex/QP active-set methods (Fletcher, Goldfarb, Nocedal-Wright); SMO recast as chunk size 2; distinguished from Cauwenberghs-Poggio and Hastie et al. path methods; sprint credited to Forrest, singular case to Belloni; S003 IPM as warm start (pp. 2-4, 17, 20).
writing: Abstract concedes 'The underlying method is not new'; scope fenced (generalization identical, not discussed); toy example (ten identical points) justifies a design choice; normative remark on overfitting problems; two-sentence conclusion; no theorems (pp. 1, 3-4, 10, 19).
limits_future: Memory for the Cholesky factor when n_s is large; iterative solver needed for extreme sizes; crude IPM in warm start; no full path; incremental mode loses look-ahead; future: theoretical analysis of behaviour and complexity, kernel-parameter warm starts, C++ version (pp. 4, 10, 13, 17, 19).

title: Geometry of interpolation sets in derivative free optimization
contribution: Introduces Lambda-poisedness (Lagrange polynomials as coefficients of phi(x) in the sample vectors), proves its equivalence up to constants with the conditioning of the scaled natural-basis interpolation matrix, derives explicit Taylor-like bounds for linear, quadratic and cubic interpolation in those terms, and gives LU/QR point-replacement algorithms with a provable poisedness bound.
problem_entry: Convergence needs a uniformly bounded geometry constant, but Powell's Lagrange maintenance has no bound, the authors' own 1997 Newton method needs expensive full-set replacement, and Ciarlet-Raviart constants are not algorithmic (pp. 2-6, 19).
key_idea: Measure geometry by ||M^-1|| / kappa(M^) of the natural-basis matrix on Y scaled to the unit ball, which is equivalent to Lambda-poisedness and can be controlled by a pivot threshold during LU or QR factorization, replacing only the points that spoil poisedness (pp. 7-8, 18-23).
assumptions: Lipschitz gradient (linear), Lipschitz Hessian (quadratic), Lipschitz third derivatives (cubic) on a neighbourhood of B(Delta); enclosing ball centred at origin and y0 = 0 wlog; determined interpolation only; no noise (pp. 2, 6, 11-14, 25).
proof_devices: Lagrange polynomials as coefficient vector lambda(x) with M^T lambda(x) = phi(x), hence basis independence (Lemma 3.1, p. 6)
norm equivalence psi(v) = max_{x in B(1)} |v^T phi(x)| >= sigma||v|| plus singular-vector orthogonality to get ||M^-1|| <= theta*Lambda (Theorem 3.3, pp. 8-9)
any quadratic with unit infinity-norm coefficients reaches >= 1/4 on B(1), by restricting to 1-2 variables (Lemma 3.4, pp. 9-10)
scale invariance of Lagrange polynomials vs non-invariance of kappa(M) (Lemma 3.5, p. 11)

error system: subtract interpolation equations from Taylor expansions at x, cancel e^f via the center point, obtain x-independent system with the scaled interpolation matrix; explicit constants (Theorems 4.1-4.2, pp. 12-17)
factorization bound ||M^-1|| <= c(p1)*eps_growth/xi with pivot threshold xi < 1/4 always attainable (Propositions 5.1-5.2, pp. 19-23)
experiments: One Matlab sanity test: 100 random points in the unit cube, sets chosen by Powell's Lagrange maximization, LU and QR give similar ||M^-1|| (mostly 10-100, never > 1000); caveats stated; no optimization runs (p. 24).
positioning: Credits Powell's strategy as reasonable and practical but unproven, applies the same criticism to own 1997 method, contrasts with Ciarlet-Raviart and de Boor, links the linear case to positive bases in pattern search; novelty claimed modestly (usefulness and simplicity over novelty of bounds) (pp. 5-6, 17-20).
writing: Intuition before theorem (distance to linear dependency), remarks after theorems, early organization paragraph, hedged practical claims (may not beat Powell's algorithm) (pp. 1, 3, 7, 10-11, 23).
limits_future: Determined interpolation only (regression/underdetermined deferred); polynomials recomputed at updates; practical value untested in a DFO package; theta for d > 2 open; future: prove Powell-like algorithms give uniform well-poisedness (pp. 2, 10, 19, 23-24), later taken up by S088/S104.
